name: Input Buffer
description: Predictive input buffering for Geometry Dash.

name: Swing Timing Style (Experimental)
description:
How clicks are handled in swing mode, using the swing window.

**Min Hold** (default): a quick tap is held for at least the window.
**Min Gap**: clicks keep at least the window between a release and the next press.
**Grid**: presses and releases snap to a fixed beat. Clicks can be delayed by up to the window, so it can make some timings impossible to hit.

Experimental. Leave on Min Hold unless you are testing.

sections.name: Level Sections (Experimental)
sections.description:
Lets a level use different settings between percents you choose (for example 0.00-35.00% one setup, 35.50-60.00% another). Each section has its own start, end and settings. Edit them from the pause menu: **Buffer > Advanced > Sections**.

Off by default. Sections do not work in platformer levels. Switching sections clears held input at the boundary.

tps-value.name: Game Speed (TPS)
tps-value.description:
Type the TPS you set in Mega Hack, or 240 if you have not changed it. Any whole number from 1 to 10000 works, for example 240, 360, 720 or 1000.

The mod uses this to turn ticks into real time. If it is wrong, every window will be the wrong size: too short if you type less than your real TPS, too long if you type more.

This does not change your game's speed. It only tells the mod what speed you are running.

debug.name: Debug Logging
debug.description: Prints detailed messages to the console about what the buffer is doing. Only useful for troubleshooting. Leave it off for normal play.

description: Switches between Min Hold, Min Gap and Grid. Best used while paused.

kb-section.name: Key: Add Section Here
kb-section.description: Adds a section to the current level at the percent you are at right now (experimental sections). Works in a level, including practice mode.

sec-experimental.name: Experimental
sec-experimental.description: Features that are still being tested. They are off by default and may not behave perfectly.

dual-mode.name: Dual Mode Support (Experimental)
dual-mode.description:
Turns the buffer on during **dual sections**: when a dual portal gives you a second icon in a normal one-player level.

**Off** (default): dual sections use the normal game input. There is no buffering or timing help while you are dual.
**On**: each icon is buffered by its own game mode, so a cube and a wave can each follow their own rules.

This is experimental and can behave unexpectedly, for example a click doing nothing on one icon, or an extra jump. If something feels wrong in a dual section, turn this off.

2-player levels are not affected by this setting.
